# Credo Technology Group (CRDO): research and conditional valuation
As of October 18, 2026. Research staging only; no publication or canonical edits. USD millions unless stated. Original analysis; no reproduced licensed transcripts. Source identifiers resolve in source-ledger-v1.json.

## Decision summary
Credo is a real US-listed AI interconnect business with extraordinary recent operating growth and unusually concentrated demand. Its investable thesis is no longer merely active copper cables: optical components, complete transceivers, and inference-memory connectivity expand the opportunity, but also expand manufacturing commitments, integration risk, and the amount of equity granted to staff and acquisition sellers. A sound valuation must fund this expansion and allocate existing claims before dividing by ordinary shares.

The base case assumes FY2027 revenue of $2.5bn, FY2031 $5.4bn and FY2036 $8.0bn. These are analyst scenarios, not consensus or a target-price inversion. The current conditional base value is about $92 per ordinary share, with a wide bear/bull span of about $39–169. The result is highly sensitive to sustained growth, durable margins, the discount rate and terminal economics. These are intrinsic scenario outputs, not price targets or recommendations. No live market quote enters the model. Public stock pages show inconsistent quote timestamps (Robinhood labels Sunday October 18 activity); therefore no precise current upside/downside percentage is asserted.

## Identity and eligibility
- Cayman incorporated parent, US Nasdaq-listed ordinary shares CRDO, $0.00005 par, not an ADR. SEC CIK 1807794. Listing verified in latest 10-Q and October16 8-K.
- Robinhood's US CRDO page explicitly offers buying/selling the stock. This is public platform eligibility, not verification of a specific user's account, jurisdiction, fractional order, extended-hours permission or suitability.
- IPO January27,2022, as reported in initial earnings release. The company was formed September2014. Ten fiscal slots FY2017–26 are supplied: seven reported annual observations FY2020–26 and explicit unavailable/private-history entries FY2017–19. No invented decade of public-company data.

## Business, economics and competition
Credo develops SerDes and DSP intellectual property, chips and system-level interconnects. AECs use active electronics to extend copper reach and improve reliability; optical DSPs and silicon-photonics PICs serve longer connections; ZeroFlap combines optical hardware, diagnostics and software. Retimers address signal degradation in Ethernet, PCIe and emerging scale-up architectures. OmniConnect addresses memory fan-out. Customer value comes from uptime, rapid cluster commissioning, power and signal integrity, rather than a commodity cable alone.

The business is fabless, but not free of reinvestment. FY2026 semiconductor wafer production was exclusively TSMC; assembly/test and cable partners include Amkor, ASE, KYEC, Sigurd and BizLink. Purchase commitments, inventory, receivables, supplier capacity deposits and technology licenses matter even when owned manufacturing capex is small. Competitors identified by Credo include Broadcom, Marvell, Astera and cable/optical module suppliers. Larger competitors can price aggressively and integrate products into broader platforms. Customer design wins can persist through a platform generation, but they are neither recurring software subscriptions nor guaranteed perpetual shares of hyperscaler spend.

Historical mix is measurable only at a broad level. FY2025 product sales plus engineering were 97% of revenue, IP licenses 3%; FY2024 85% and15%. Latest financial statements do not provide an exact audited AEC/optics/retimer revenue split. The scenario model does not disguise estimates as reported segment data. One reportable segment is not evidence of one homogeneous economic product.

Concentration must be measured on the right basis. FY2026 top10 contracting customers represented approximately90% of sales. FY2026 end-customer concentrations were33%,32%,19%; Q1FY2027 end-customer shares were33%,28%,13%,10%. Contracting customers in Q1 were43% and28%, which can include manufacturers ordering on an end customer's behalf. Do not identify anonymous lettered customers with named companies or sum the two bases. Geography is destination of shipment: the US accounted for$255.442m of Q1 sales, Hong Kong$91.175m, Malaysia$74.455m and mainland China$1.095m. Those figures do not identify ultimate AI users or justify mechanically applying shipment-country equity risk premiums.

## Management evidence, including contrary evidence
Sources include all annual filings FY2022–26, every public 10-Q located since IPO, the IPO S-1, earnings releases from FY2022Q3 onward, and material recent 8-Ks. The latest financial information is the quarter ended August1, filed September2. October16's 8-K concerns annual meeting votes, not newer balances.

September1 FY2027Q1 call, original summary (management testimony hosted by StockAnalysis): management expects FY2027 sales growth above85%, optical revenue above$600m, with each of DSPs, PICs and ZeroFlap exceeding$100m. AECs remain the largest business. It expects new NPO, ALC and OmniConnect contributions in FY2028. In Q&A, management emphasized customer-specific deployment patterns and supply preparation; working capital is increasing to support the optics ramp. The fourth10% customer changed from the prior quarter. Non-GAAP FY2027 opex is expected to rise roughly55% and gross margin to remain broadly comparable to FY2026. These statements are forecasts, not purchase commitments. Source: Q1FY27 call, prepared remarks and Q&A.

September10 Goldman conference, original summary: Brennan described a medium-agnostic connectivity strategy. Reliability and power efficiency, not the copper-versus-optics label, are the proposed competitive advantage. He described optical execution as a key source of upside and cautioned that individual hyperscalers surge and pause on different schedules. Management testimony mentions historical work with xAI, Oracle and Microsoft; this does not authorize mapping them to anonymous filing concentration percentages. Source: CEO September10 interview.

CEO presentation evidence: the 17-page GSA-hosted Interconnect Wall deck frames network failure frequency as a growing cluster-level problem, outlines AECs, optical transceivers, telemetry and memory gearboxes, and describes several addressable markets. Its engineering/TAM assumptions are company claims, not audited unit economics. Filename suggests November2025, but event date was not independently confirmed; no quantitative forecast relies on that date or its TAM. October13 company commentary on Brennan's OCP presentation introduces the 1.6T active-light-cable direction and short-reach micro-emitter standardization. This is useful strategic evidence, not proof of booked revenue or achieved third-party reliability.

The contiguous guide-versus-actual panel covers18 quarters, FY2022Q4–FY2027Q1, across revenue, GAAP/non-GAAP gross margin and opex. Original quarter-ahead ranges remain the benchmarks. FY2026Q3's February9 preliminary raise to$404–408m is recorded separately from its original$335–345m outlook; eventual$407m is not counted as a beat of a newly lowered hurdle.

Important misses and qualifications:
- FY2022Q4 revenue$37.5m was inside$37–41m but below midpoint; GAAP opex exceeded the range.
- FY2023Q2 gross margin54.4% missed58.5–60.5% despite revenue meeting guidance.
- FY2023Q3 revenue$54.3m was below the$55m midpoint; opex exceeded guide.
- The repeated FY2023 annual outlook of at least$200m missed at$184.194m (7.9% below the floor). February14,2023 disclosed a largest-customer demand cut and reset FY2024 to roughly flat. FY2024 eventually grew4.8%, illustrating how near-term beats can coexist with a serious original annual miss.
- FY2027Q1 revenue$479m exceeded$465–475m, but GAAP gross margin64.5% missed66.9–68.9%, and GAAP opex$188.4m exceeded$167.6–171.6m. Non-GAAP opex$95.2m exceeded$86–90m too. Acquisition timing and stronger R&D investment complicate like-for-like comparisons; they do not erase the deviation.
- Several actuals are rounded to$0.1m in press releases. Borderline high-end results can differ at full precision. These are management-guide comparisons, never analyst-consensus surprise statistics.

## Financial history and comparability
history-v1.csv/json provides revenue, gross profit, EBIT, net income, tax, CFO, capex, D&A, SBC, R&D, balances and share measures. history-field-provenance-v1.json records the individual SEC tag, period, accession, filing date and unit behind each value. Fiscal year is assigned from the actual period end, not the SEC companyfacts fiscal-year label of a later comparative filing. Latest comparative observations available by cutoff are selected; this is not an as-originally-reported backtest.

Revenue rose from$53.835m inFY2020 to$1335.116m inFY2026. EBIT was negative inFY2021–24, positive$37.124m inFY2025 and$445.005m inFY2026. FY2026 CFO$464.292m less capex$57.296m yields$406.996m. This cash metric adds back$182.638m SBC and is not equivalent to shareholder FCFF after compensation economics.

Q1FY2027 revenue$479.003m, GAAP EBIT$120.700m and SBC$87.979m yield a very different operating picture from non-GAAP profitability. CFO$90.231m less capex$7.282m was$82.949m. Inventory rose to$313.051m and receivables to$288.798m. TTM revenue is$1591.045m; TTM EBIT$504.963m; TTM SBC$235.162m. These exact bridges are validated.

Comparability caveats: FY2023 adopted a52/53-week convention instead of calendar-month quarter ends; FY2025 is53weeks. The IPO converts the pre-public capital structure, so early per-share figures are not normalized public returns. FY2025's$13.186m warrant contra-revenue is fully amortized by year-end; FY2026 has none. Acquisition accounting expands goodwill/intangibles and amortization. Historical cash flow includes financing and equity compensation effects. Changes in customer mix, shipment mix and product-versus-IP mix limit mechanical margin extrapolation.

## Acquisition and claims bridge
DustPhotonics closed May28,2026. Latest purchase accounting totals$1251.111m: cash$769.587m, issued ordinary shares$169.069m, replacement-award pre-combination services$2.455m, and contingent consideration$310m. Net cash acquired makes the investing cash payment$735.619m. The contingent amount comprises$10m liability and$300m equity. Acquisition-date goodwill is$895.839m and identifiable intangibles$361.7m. These are preliminary purchase allocations. Paid cash and already-issued shares are already in August balances and must not be subtracted or diluted twice.

The April agreement specifies up to approximately3.21m contingent shares. Since current fair value and milestone probabilities are not publicly observed, the base scenario uses an explicit conditional expected-share proxy:300/(222.35×3.21)=approximately42.0% of the maximum, calibrated to acquisition-date equity fair value and reference share price. This is not an observed vesting probability or a current fair value. Bear20%, bull100%, and0–100% sensitivity are retained. We allocate expected shares against intrinsic equity value rather than subtracting both$300m and the full contingent shares. The$10m cash liability is deducted once.

The old Amazon customer warrant was fully exercised by May2,2026: approximately4.1m warrant shares produced net issuance3.8m after exercise-price withholding. No live warrant claim from that agreement is deducted. Mixing Astera's newer warrant with Credo would be an error.

August1 has187.768m ordinary shares,8.3m RSUs,3.1m PSUs and1.7m options at$2.34 weighted strike and3.84years remaining. August25 cover shares are187.951918m. Neither186.007m basic weighted-average nor194.378m diluted weighted-average Q1 EPS shares is the point-in-time denominator. The model's dated balance snapshot uses187.768m; the current bridge explicitly estimates188.468m with corresponding reduction in outstanding RSUs.

RSUs vest at an analyst95% assumption. Scenario PSU vesting factors35%/65%/100% apply to the3.1m pool, not an observed probability. The May28 special CEO grant comprises1.437m PSUs in six239,500-share tranches, with paired trailing-revenue hurdles$2.5bn to$7.5bn and stock-price hurdles$244.70 to$489.40 through June2031. First two tranches can partly vest without the stock hurdle; service and change-of-control terms matter. These award hurdles are not company revenue guidance or guaranteed dilution. The base probability is intentionally conditional and should be replaced by a full path-dependent award valuation when suitable grant-level data are available. Maximum-count sensitivity is more honest than pretending the grant-date fair value is today's claim.

Options are valued with Black-Scholes inside an equity-allocation fixed point. Volatility78.62% is a disclosed FY2026 ESPP assumption used as an explicitly imperfect proxy, with55–95% sensitivity. Deep in-the-money low-strike options make this proxy much less important than the revenue/margin case. A0.132m exchangeable subsidiary restricted-share allowance is also included; parent restricted shares already issued are not added again. Acquisition replacement RSUs are treated as included in the total RSU rollforward, not added separately.

## DCF construction and assumption rationale
This is a ten-year FCFF DCF with calendar-aware remainingFY2027 stub, explicit annual revenue, margins, taxes, reinvestment, discount rates and terminal reinvestment. replay_dcf.py reads only the versioned inputs and needs Python's standard library. No market price is used to calibrate results.

Revenue: baseFY2027$2500m is just above management's >85% growth threshold ($2469.965m). With actualQ1$479.003m and Q2 midpoint$530m, it requires$1490.997m in the second half. That is demanding and depends on optics scaling; Q2 guide alone does not prove it. FY2028$3250m reflects broader optics and initial memory/ALC contributions; FY2029$4000m andFY2030$4720m assume continued penetration but decelerating growth; FY2031$5400m is modestly above the$5bn strategic-plan reference in the CEO award disclosure. Subsequent growth fades to5% byFY2036. Bear assumes delayed optics and concentration-driven slowdown; bull assumes successful new-platform ramps across a substantially wider market. None of these revenues is presented as booked backlog.

Margins: starting cash operating margins before new equity labor are42%/46%/49% for bear/base/bull; base fades to42%. These are anchored below/near recent adjusted operating profitability, with competition and product mix absorbing scale benefits. New post-valuation awards are charged as a cash-equivalent10% of revenue, fading to8%. Base economic operating margin is thus36% initially and34% inFY2036. Existing-award amortization is excluded because the associated outstanding claims are allocated separately. Do not add future SBC back again or use diluted EPS shares on top. These are economic replacement-cost assumptions, not predictions of GAAP presentation. R&D remains expensed throughout; no fictitious research asset or duplicate R&D capex is added.

Tax: recent GAAP tax is exceptionally low and the latest quarter has an acquisition-related benefit. The model does not capitalize a negative tax rate forever. Base cash tax fades6%→18%; bear reaches21%, bull18%. No separate NOL asset is added, preventing a second benefit. Jurisdictional taxable income and future policy remain uncertain.

Reinvestment: incremental revenue divided by marginal sales/capital, initially1.8/2.2/2.6 across scenarios. Base early2.2 is conservative versus a naïve fabless capex-only extrapolation: inventories, receivables and deposits consume capital. Late-stage base turns fade2.0,1.6,1.2,0.9,0.65 as easy penetration gives way to replacement investment and mature capital economics. Terminal ROIC12%/15%/20% requires reinvestment g/ROIC, rather than zero-capex perpetual growth. Base terminal3% growth implies20% of NOPAT reinvested and an incremental terminal sales/capital ratio near0.538, directionally continuous with the last explicit year. Past acquisition price is sunk as of the balance date; future incremental capital includes ongoing platform renewal, not a free repetition of acquired growth.

Capacity timing: the post-August1 commitment to$102.4m additional refundable supplier deposits is modeled as an extra first-stub use, with equal$25.6m recoveries inFY2028–31. These represent timing capital over and above ordinary capital turns; they are not an additional permanent acquisition expense. Return timing and collectability are assumptions. Existing$88.4m deposits remain operating assets, not surplus cash. Ordinary$212.717m inventory commitments are funded through operating costs/reinvestment, not subtracted again as debt. Technology-license obligations$9.495m are debt-like and deducted; operating lease costs remain in margins, with no separate lease-debt subtraction.

WACC: Treasury10-year5.09% onOctober16 and Damodaran October1 ERP4.20% are dated primary-source inputs. Analyst beta1.55 gives initial11.60%, fading to beta1 and9.29% terminal. No material funded borrowing is reported, so debt weight is zero. The beta is a risk judgment, not an invented regression. Treasury/ERP are both unadjusted for the US default spread, consistently. The older snapshot uses September inputs4.75% and4.14%. Geography is not used as a mechanical country-risk adjustment. Scenario cash flows, beta and sensitivities reflect concentration, manufacturing and technology uncertainty without asserting an observed premium.

## Dates, bridge and limits
The report snapshot is an August1 balance-date valuation with information available through September2, using the subsequent report's disclosed results and guidance. It is a dated latest-report reconstruction, not a tradable August1 backtest. Current October18 scenarios remove78/273 of the remainingFY2027 operating stub and shorten discounting. They estimate net cash increase$40m and ordinary-share increase0.7m, with matching reduction in RSUs. Cash estimate:$135m operating cash after ordinary working capital, minus$15m capital expenditures,$55m capacity deposits and$25m net withholding. None is a reported October balance. The$55m paid-deposit assumption is removed from remaining-stub outflows so it is not charged twice.

The cash bridge is deliberately approximate; unlike the reported August25 share figure, post-August activity is unobserved. New grants, exercise mixes, award forfeitures, stock-price-dependent withholding and acquisition settlement timing could change it. Its dollar sensitivity is small relative to long-duration operating assumptions, but it should still be refreshed at the next filing. Remaining-stub earnings/reinvestment are allocated by estimated remaining revenue and elapsed calendar fraction, rather than pretending interim monthly operating data are available. A full quarterly cash-flow plan could improve this timing approximation.

## What would change the conclusion
Watch FY2027Q2 actual sales against$525–535m; optical growth and cash conversion; margin versus62.9–64.9% GAAP and67–69% adjusted; R&D/opex against guidance; customer concentration and order timing; supplier deposits/inventory versus capacity usage; new design wins converting into recognized revenue; and incremental equity awards. Do not infer sales from product launch headlines.

Precise remaining gaps: exact latest product-line mix, anonymous-customer identity mapping, DustPhotonics earnout milestone schedule/probabilities, complete grant-level PSU path terms and current fair values, October cash/share balances, post-August new awards and financing, and the reliability of medium-term new-product adoption. These do not force an EV-only output: conditional equity values and sensitivities are supplied, with observed facts separated from estimates. Before publication, perform an independent source/assumption review and refresh any elapsed market inputs. Arithmetic replay is not that review.
